report.summary: Analyzed chunk 7 of graph_delta.py: defines _refs_by_function and function_deltas.

handoff.purpose: Defines two functions: _refs_by_function (private) and function_deltas (public) for computing reference deltas.

symbols.name: _refs_by_function
symbols.note: Private function, not exported. Walks AST to collect reference counters per function.

symbols.name: function_deltas
symbols.note: Public function. Returns list of dicts for functions changed between two code strings.

claims.text: One row per function that exists in BOTH versions and changed.
claims.why: The function iterates over the intersection of function names from both versions.

claims.text: Functions added or removed wholesale are excluded: a new function has no 'before' to lose references against, and counting it as a huge addition would swamp the distribution the rule is read from.
claims.why: Only names present in both fb and fa are considered; the loop uses set(fb) & set(fa).

claims.text: Qualify by line so two same-named methods in one file stay distinct.
claims.why: The code uses node.name directly without line number qualification: out[f"{node.name}"] = ... This does not include any line info, so same-named methods are merged.

observations.what: The comment claims line qualification, but the code does not implement it.
